chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Lays al-Muradi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Al-Kibr (Pride/Arrogance) is the Gown of Allah. So whoever disputes with Allah regarding anything from that, Allah will cast him into the Fire.

key_terms.رِدَاءُ اللَّهِ: The Gown of Allah (a metaphor for a unique divine attribute)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of arrogance in Shia hadith and its consequence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies arrogance as the exclusive 'garment' of Allah, distinguishing divine majesty from human pride. This definition implies that arrogance is not merely a behavioral flaw but a theological usurpation of God's unique status, a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegesis where claiming equality with the Divine is the essence of kibr. The warning of being cast into the Fire underscores the severity of this attribute as a primary cause of damnation in Islamic eschatology.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Lays Al Murady, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Pride is a Gown of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. So the one who disputes Allah<sup>azwj</sup> regarding anything from that, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Fling him into the Fire’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn Ali from abu Jamilah from Lath al-Muradi from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Pride is the gown of Allah and whoever disputes Allah in anything about it, Allah will throw him into the fire.”
